### Square I
The vertical midpoint segment meets the diagonal at the center. Each shaded right triangle has legs of length \(1\), so each has area
\[
\frac12(1)(1)=\frac12.
\]
Thus
\[
A_I=\frac12+\frac12=1=\frac14(4).
\]

### Square II
The horizontal and vertical midpoint segments divide the square into four \(1\times1\) squares. Two are shaded, so
\[
A_{II}=2(1)=2=\frac12(4).
\]

### Square III
The red diamond has vertices at the side midpoints. Its horizontal and vertical diagonals both have length \(2\), so its area is
\[
A_{III}=\frac12(2)(2)=2=\frac12(4).
\]
(The black diagonals merely subdivide this shaded region.)

Therefore,
\[
A_I=1,\qquad A_{II}=A_{III}=2,
\]
so only the shaded areas in II and III are equal.

\[
\boxed{\text{D: Only the shaded areas of II and III are equal.}}
\]
